开发商的前作两个游戏经常能够在捆绑包看见，那个时候就就很感兴趣，但无中文便也就懒得去硬吃了。最近偶然在找独游时的捆绑包看见了出了2代有中文，于是便在第一时间买来体验了。[spoiler] 不过不知道是国内没有宣发还是因为尖塔2的发售吸走了绝大部分肉鸽玩家的目光，在我购买时一条中文评论也没有（发测评时倒已经有了一两条），其实说GG2也很好玩 [/spoiler] 如果要用简洁的话来概括《基因守卫者2》的话：[strike] 它是一代的Plus版 [/strike]，它是Noita/法术编程加类幸的模式。可以稍微总评一下游戏，GG2本身是建立在前作已经验证的ACTG基因组合的玩法基础上的一个更加精致的更大体量的打磨版本。 GG2的核心玩法主要为类幸或者说弹幕射击，玩家通过[spoiler]最多[/spoiler]4个武器糟和数个配件糟的“法杖”/枪管，通过将ACTG四种核酸放入武器糟以及特殊的修正放入配件糟来搭配、组合武器。 说实话类似的玩法在Noita大火（不是）后实际上并不罕见[spoiler] ，但GG2它不一样啊（） [/spoiler]。但GG2属于其中佼佼者中的佼佼者，不需要拿其深度已经去和Noita或者其他佳作来比肩才能体现GG2的优秀，因为GG2是属于很有特色的游戏[spoiler] 或者说整个系列的特色 [/spoiler]，也就是所谓的独游味。 GG2的设计十分有记忆点，其整体架构是建立于ACTG的基因的抽象，实际上在游戏中体现来看可以说是红黄蓝绿。其武器由ACTG模块组成，最多四个，不考虑先后顺序，总计是69种武器。从基础武器也就是单个ACTG种的一个来看，红色为冲锋枪，蓝色为手枪，黄色为大炮，绿色为霰弹。其中的特质基本上可以在这几种类型中体现，而组合他们就可以获得一种特质上的直观叠加的效果，[spoiler] 这就是GG2的特色，直观， [/spoiler]比如说多个红色可以获得更快的射速，多个绿色可以获得更多的子弹，多个红色加绿色就是多子弹加多射速。当然如此看会略显无趣，但实际上每一把武器除此之外还有其他的特性，同时在当你看见时很轻松的就可以接受其是由之前的武器融合"进化"得来的。逐渐探索每一个武器的特色也是游戏的乐趣所在也就不多说了。 同时GG2的敌人也是基于类似的逻辑，同样的ACTG最多四个的组合，虽然类幸的敌人大多是属于背景板的存在，但是GG2确实是让其有了鲜明的特色。基于其颜色代表特性的逻辑，红色的敌人会有更快的速度但低生命，归于其”颜色等于能力，颜色”球“越多代表能力越强“这一套易于理解接受逻辑，哪怕是从1-4红如此的叠加也显得很有意思。 在大概了解可能的方向后，依旧会有一种很想探究不同的组合的实际效果，并且在游戏中得到一个合乎情理但又有一些超脱的有意思的机制作为实际呈现的获得感真的很棒。 其次游戏有着超乎寻常的BD系统，包括数个不同部位的炮台、角色、核心、“遗物”、武器、武器配件等层面，而且绝大部分是属于局外带入，只有武器、武器配件、核心配件三个是局内BD，使得不会显得臃肿，反而有一种各种妙妙机制来量大管饱，而且作为EA体量已经足够夸张。[spoiler] 此游也有蓝色鸡煲 [/spoiler] 然后作为前作没有的本地化，体验实属不赖，文本十分趣味，并非字典版的详细定义，而是一种向冒险家介绍魔物小故事的幽默，虽然也可以说是不够明确。[spoiler] 反正我个人更喜欢（） [/spoiler] 然后游戏的色彩作为一大特色，但是建议一定要先去设置调低饱和度，不然真的纯粹光污染。不得不说游戏的优化非常不赖，相当高强度的弹幕完全不卡。[spoiler] 4060笔记本 [/spoiler] 总而言之Genome Guardian 2是一款真正精致的独立佳作，完全值得抽出爬塔的时间来注入基因，如果你愿意的话~

Doesn't really stand out in the genre. There's a lot of fluff - I'd normally say that as a good thing, but this game is pretty bare-bones gameplay-wise. I find it's more like an idler or Vampire Survivors-like than a twin stick shooter. You don't really have to pay attention, usually. I didn't hate it, but once you get over the flashing colors you're stuck with a claustrophobic and samey experience. I hope the dev abandons the tiny circle arena thing, as movement is an afterthought at this point. With a bigger arena/obstacles there could be a broadening of gameplay as well. The breadth of the genepool is really expressed in something like Cell Command, where movement matters and maps impact you in some way.

Provided for free for content creation on launch, this review is not paid in any way and this is my personal thoughts of Genome Guardian as a whole. I DO NOT UNDERSTAND why people do not play this game. Genome Guardian 1 and 2 are easily the most unique survivors games of all time, easily passing through titles such as Vampire Survivors and 20 Minutes TIll Dawn. Im sorry to break it for you, but thoose games are a sad sob compared to both Genome entries. Super fun, short, bite sized, keeps your attention, LOTS of accessibility options, LOTS to grind for, LOTS to buy, LOTS of variety, UNIQUE characters, UNIQUE features. DO I HAVE TO KEEP GOING??? For example, the Boombox Guardian (Guardians are the characters) scales its size, firerate and damage depending on how the ingame music is playing. If it goes loud and wild, it does damage, if its a simple song, 0 attributes. Just this Guardian should be a main reason to buy this sequel because the game literally encourages you to mix up a good playlist just to play with this specific character. Also the new JESTER Guardian was a fun thing to play, but after winning i dont want to use him anymore...Its just a weird ride. This game also has multiple games in it, similar to Stick It To The Stickman. Depths also add actual difficulty and the only complaint i have is too much hand holding, except for that this game is a masterpiece and again: The best survivors game of all time. You also have Parts, Mods, Gadgets and Weapons, each with their own unique feature. The main part of the game is the weapons, which are DNA letters where you can mix them for 60+ variations and basically infinite build variety. What can i say? This is peak.
I know the "Jester" guardian is meant to be joke, but opening a web browser to a random link unprompted seems risky. All other aspects seem good, but opening links unwarranted just sours the game.

I have played through the three modes available, and all I have to say is that I cannot wait for this to be fully released. I could put hundreds of hours into this game already as it stands. Absolutely masterclass execution of a roguelike. Instead of talking about what is there though, I want to talk about what I still want in the game, because right now it's still in Early Access and I'd love to see some things done before the full release: - Freeze doesn't work like I expect it to, and it can really feel kinda janky as a status effect as a result. Due to the freeze effect being directly related to the HP of a microbe, you have to pair it with high damage effects to get the slowing results that you want. However, this breaks down greatly in something like a Maw build, where I want my primary damage to come from eating microbes, and only use the freeze effect to slow down microbes. See the issue? High damage from the freeze weapon will kill, depriving our Maw build of nutrients, which means the Maw build won't benefit from freeze weapons at all as it stands currently (rather ironically). A laborious fix to this issue (but probably one of the better methods) might be to have freeze buildup be a separate stat based on how many hits a microbe has received by a freezing-type projectile during the last 5 seconds, slowing the microbe with each hit down to a floor (fully frozen). This change would enable builds that intentionally go for low damage and high status-effect buildup, relying on the Maw (or other future Guardian abilities) for main damage delivery. The freeze chip (frozen microbe speed -30%) would lower that slowness floor further, bringing slower microbes to a near-stop as opposed to the crawl they'd normally reach at max freeze (fully frozen), with two chips bringing all microbes that get sufficiently frozen (even the more speedy ones) to a dead stop. Of course, you can't be frozen if you're dead, so you can see why this would benefit lower-damage weapon builds and even intentionally seeking lower damage. Of course, you could also have it be BOTH tied to HP AND a separate build-up meter both, intensifying freezing effects on lower HP% targets. - Some other status effects don't apply attached effects, and I really wish they did. I really wish my zaps could also burn or freeze what is being zapped for example, or my burns could apply freeze buildup. (Or that my zaps could apply burns that build up freeze...) Only a projectile can currently apply a status like burn, freeze, or stun from my observations... I can hear the question already: How would the order of application be decided? Build order is the obvious answer; if the effect comes from a Guardian, it's going to apply first and foremost, followed by build part effects. Then mods will come into consideration in the order they were installed. Then arsenal weapon effects themselves (the description effects in order of listing in their description; like CGGT coming with zap followed by flak - the zap will be applied to the flak projectiles), followed by the genes attached to the weapons. Gadget status effects obviously are their own thing though. I think this is a critical thing keeping some of my builds from truly popping off when it looks like on the book that they should be doing fine. - I'd love a zap related modification that makes zap link up between fired groupings of projectiles instead of between nearby microbes and applies damage to everything between those projectiles; combining this effect with chaotic burst missile weapons or a shotgun and the tazer to make walls and webs of electricity that continuously stun enemies would be a truly sick combo. - I'm itching for a motherboard or two that allows for a fourth chip installation during a run to get real silly with. If not added to a board coming in the future, then F-0CU5 and H0-7D06 would both be good options for this addition, with some tweaks. In a similar vein, a motherboard that enabled a 5th mod would also be awesome. A secret board with both options would be a dream. I'd expect some balance changes for sure if such things were to exist. A man can dream. - I'm also hoping for more brutality in the full release to compensate for all of the nuttiness I'm asking for here: 10 depths instead of 5. Ramp it up like crazy in the later depths. Increase spawn rates and wave times. Increase the arena size by scaling everybody down and slowing their movement speed both equally to allow for more spawns! Make it feel like I'm pushing the absolute limits of Nanobot tech here. Introduce behavior events in the lower depths that make random mutations (like Hysteria, Stillborn, Charge, etc.) suddenly activate on their own for a wave and then deactivate. Also, introduce shop genes that allow the player to mutate their own weapon builds (like mutating a CCCG into an ACCG) in depths 6-10. The later depths should only be unlocked when all non-secret parts, guardians, mods, weapon combinations, and gadgets have been discovered and all depths 1-5 of all modes have been completed; they should be hidden prior to that. - Along this vein, I'm keen to see bosses (aka Abyssal Horrors) implemented someday - perhaps in these later depths. Boss waves with mutated abyss versions of known microbes with massive HP, upgraded attacks, special AI with phases, and whatnot would go hard. Seeing these mutants fire back at us trying to destroy us... Shooting AOEs that we have to dodge and needing to navigate summoned minion microbes... Managing being burned, frozen, or zapped ourselves... You get the gist. There's potential for much more even yet... - Having all microbes unlocked in the database should unlock the ability to see the types of microbes that are going to spawn in the next wave during the shop. In earlier depths, this wouldn't matter too much, but on depths 6-10 where bosses could show up and weapons can be mutated to address the situation, it becomes much more relevant. Otherwise, I'm just excited for more, and will still be dumping a ton of time into this game in the future; the replayability and the number of builds possible keep pulling me back in, and will probably do so for the foreseeable future. It's Genome Guardian with even more stuff. If you played the first Genome Guardian, you already know that's a really good thing. If you haven't: this game is a roguelite wave survival game with a weapon fusion & upgrade system that gives you a million bajillion different options for powering up your weapons during a run, on top of a million bajillion different options for your character/perks/etc on a run-to-run basis. These options are substantial, some to the point of creating an entirely unique playstyle. If you like experimenting with different bonuses, mixing and matching stuff to see what happens and how strong you can get, you'll probably like this game. Also, the dev (solo dev, I think? forgive me if I'm wrong) presents information in-game in a way that's very candid and, at times, witty, which I really appreciate - I like when games kinda pull down the veil between the developer and player and talk to the player directly, makes it feel more... "human", I guess? Anyways, in summary, this is an excellent sequel to a game that was already excellent.

At the very least, AI translation should be used.

If you're like, "man, I wish I could capture the magic of games like Centipede or Space Invaders but with all the bells and whistles of modernity and basically infinite replayability through both roguelite progression and just sheer volume of things to do" -- you're home. Install. Thank us all later in the Discord. If you're not thinking that, I ... hunh. I guess you're too young to remember Centipede and Space Invaders? That's adorable. Buy this game, it's, uh... it's like if Geometry Dash took the drugs your parents keep telling you are bad. Which, like, don't do those, they're bad. But this game isn't? Yeah.

Straightforward twin-stick roguelite with loads of combinations for equipment and their effects. Has quite an amount of options for adjusting the game to taste. You can even turn it into a Survivors-like with separate options for auto-aim AND auto-fire. It's like Crimsonland and Brotato had a baby. Killing things without interruption, mess with your build inbetween waves. Some "characters" can't move while others are quite mobile in their own ways. There's metaprogression in two different ways. 1) Incremental changes such as + damage, accuracy, more rerolls, etc. And 2) Parts to permanently unlock that you can toy around with. This can get rather intricate, so they've even included a generous loadout system with a ton of save slots. You can disable the screen shaking and vibrations or even turn it all the way up. It's quite trippy and gets you in a groove, though can be a little bit of an eyestrain over lengthy play.
